text:
Predicates:
Taller(x, y) ::: x is taller than y.
Blocks(x, y) ::: x can block y's shooting.
Jumps(x) ::: x jumps when shooting.
GreatShooter(x) ::: x is a great shooter.
Person(x) ::: x is a person.
Michael ::: Michael.
Windy ::: Windy.
Peter ::: Peter.
Class(x) ::: x is in Michael's class.
Premises:
∀x ∀y (Taller(x, y) → Blocks(x, y)) ::: If x is taller than y, then x can block y's shooting.
Taller(Michael, y) ∀y (Class(y)) ::: Michael is taller than everyone in his class.
∀x ∀y ∀z ((Taller(x, y) ∧ Taller(y, z)) → Taller(x, z)) ::: If x is taller than y and y taller than z, then x is taller than z.
Taller(Peter, Michael) ::: Peter is taller than Michael.
∀x (Jumps(x) → GreatShooter(x)) ::: Anyone who jumps when shooting is a great shooter.
¬Blocks(Michael, Windy) ::: Michael cannot block Windy's shooting.
Peter ::: Person.
Windy ::: Person.
Michael ::: Person.
Premises:
Taller(Peter, Michael) ::: Peter is taller than Michael.
Jumps(Windy) ::: Windy jumps when shooting.
Conclusion:
¬Blocks(Peter, Windy) ::: Peter cannot block Windy's shooting.
